paragraphs.text: Loose [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Yunnan, made in the 1990s and kept in Guangzhou since. It was never pressed into a cake, so the leaf has aged loose, with more air around it than a cake or brick allows.

The leaf went through the [wet pile](shou:wet-piling) that Yunnan’s state factories brought into production in 1973. At thirty-one years it is well past the ten-year mark the trade uses for [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged), and where it was stored has shaped it as much as the years have.

brewing.text: Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
